queries.query: Julian of Norwich sees all of creation as a small round thing no bigger than a hazelnut resting in her hand, and learns it endures only because God made it, loves it, and keeps it
queries.note: The hazelnut shewing; 'the quantity of an hazel-nut in the palm of my hand', 'it is all that is made', 'fallen to naught for littleness' paraphrased away; 'hazelnut' kept — the image any reader of Julian knows.

queries.query: Julian wonders why God did not prevent sin at the beginning, and is comforted that sin plays a necessary part yet every kind of thing will be made well in the end
queries.note: The 'sin is behovable but all shall be well' shewing; 'behovable', 'the beginning of sin was not hindered' and the fourfold 'I may/can/will/shall make all thing well' paraphrased away.

queries.query: the vision-parable shown to Julian of a lord with a single servant who rushes off eagerly on his errand, falls and lies hurt, and receives from his master not blame but a greater reward
queries.note: The example of the Lord and the Servant; 'shewed full mistily a wonderful example', 'his affright and his dread, his hurt and his maim' paraphrased away; 'lord' and 'servant' kept as the names by which readers know the parable.

queries.query: where Julian describes Jesus as our true Mother, feeding and rearing souls with the tenderness of a wise mother who knows her child's need
queries.note: The Motherhood-of-Christ chapters; 'Kind Mother, Gracious Mother', 'forthspreading', 'witteth and knoweth the need of her child' paraphrased away; 'Mother' itself kept — it is the doctrine's name.

queries.query: how can a good and almighty God permit the great harm that evil does to his creatures
queries.note: Julian's anguished 'how might all be well?'; theodicy is answered by nearly every tradition in the corpus. No target — graded post-hoc.

queries.query: why pray at all if God has already ordained everything that will happen
queries.note: 'I am the Ground of thy beseeching' — prayer under providence; a question many traditions answer. No target — graded post-hoc.
